g.data-label: 4 · every logical LedgerEvent reaches the returned trace — the obligation is PARITY, not a shared transition where the substrate permits it, append and project in one transition: that is the strongest form and the default stream emissions are the named exception · the provider callback's closed effect row means projection happens during the call and the append happens after it returns, so one shared transition is impossible by construction (D1) · for that class the obligation is discharged by an explicitly checked invariant instead — projected sequence and returned emission log must match exactly in order and content, no duplicate, no omission an external ledger_emit call is not evidence the event is in LedgerTrace; the returned trace is authoritative

g.data-label: 6 · a mismatch, invalid program, exhausted stream, or forbidden effect is a HarnessFailure — but only where the runner can observe it a profile-routing or exclusion violation detected inside the runner can return a typed value, because the driver is still running a raw capability bypass cannot: a denied ambient effect terminates evaluation, so no typed result and no partial trace exists to return · that case is an expected non-zero run, and the two must not be conflated in the contract or in the probes that test it requiring both to return the same typed value needs an effect-interposition mechanism that preserves the driver-owned partial trace, proven on the pinned substrate first — none exists today

g.data-label: the event vocabulary is a versioned artifact, and the fifth recorded axis one artifact binds, for every LedgerEvent variant: the variant · its wire name · its payload schema · and its classification as logical or display-only — the distinction contract item 4 and D7's parity invariant both depend on, and which exists nowhere today at HEAD the vocabulary has 34 variants whose wire names live in trailing source comments rather than in a type, and whose consumer is a switch in a separate TypeScript process — a mapping that can drift silently, and once the returned trace is the oracle it must not

g.data-label: this is new construction; nothing in the repo is a partial implementation the one naming function that exists — phase_vocab.ail:561 ledger_record_name — names 3 of the 34 variants and collapses the other 31 to the literal string 'wire' · it is not a seed that can be grown into the artifact, it is a different thing that happens to share a subject the vertical spike found this the hard way: its check that RunSummary is the final record could not be written against it and needed a bespoke matcher validated at load, fails closed on an unclassified variant · the preferred form derives the wire name from the type, making drift a compile error and the inventory regenerable · a change to any variant, wire name, payload schema, or classification is a version change, under D8's rule for old programs: preserve decoding or pin a runner, never silently reinterpret the plan must not schedule any D7 parity invariant or acceptance row that depends on the classification before the artifact exists — those checks are undecidable until it does

g.data-label: D7 · invariants over the whole execution exactly one final RunSummary, and none synthesized for a harness failure · parity between all logical emissions and returned records · legal phase and state transitions · valid tool-call/result pairing including denial and failure paths · monotonically valid budget and cost accounting · bounded retry and progress under the modeled fault catalogue · checkpoint and compaction history invariants · outcome/summary agreement · strict-replay request equality, safe regression compatibility, and complete interaction consumption · valid logical-world transitions including declared commit/no-commit under faults · monotonic virtual time and deadline derivation · zero generator failures, matcher mismatches, forbidden effects, and ambient RNG reads the discovery contract is itself an invariant: under the same manifest and profile, schema, generator id/version, seed, and initial_world run twice must produce the same resolved program, interaction log, outcome, and normalized trace liveness claims must be bounded and operational — 'terminates or reaches a named retry bound within N decisions' — not an unbounded run

g.data-label: the reproducibility promise, stated precisely discovery under the recorded manifest, profile, and seed reproduces the same resolved program · the exact program reproduces the same normalized interaction log, outcome, and trace · under a newer revision the program remains the same regression input, and a changed outcome may be the intended evidence a bug was fixed — replay does not promise identical output across code changes · a schema migration preserves old-program decoding or provides a pinned runner any PRNG, draw-order, range, boundary-strategy, or default-initial-world change that can remap a seed requires a generator-version bump, enforced by a pinned canary per stable generator id shrinking operates on programs, preserving causality and revalidating after every reduction · it may land after the first gate if the deferral is recorded, but replay of the unshrunk failing program is not optional

tspan.tspan: the reproducibility promise, stated precisely

g.data-label: D11 · the two corpora and their counters a blocking PR corpus of fixed seeds and exact promoted regression programs, plus a scheduled rotating corpus whose seed window changes deterministically each declares an operator-accepted minimum the gate asserts exactly — zero, silently truncated, or below-minimum fails class-reached and branch-reached are separate counters read from D3's catalogue: reaching a fault class is not evidence the production branch it targets executed, and only the second is the coverage the acceptance test asks for · every waived class is reported with the condition that waived it a scheduled failure is promoted together with the execution manifest it ran under, and the two travel as one artifact · D8's promise is conditioned on that manifest, so a program promoted without one is a program nobody can state the meaning of · a stale or unresolvable manifest is never silently reinterpreted: strict replay fails closed, regression replay proceeds only with the difference recorded
